subject: Logic
title: Medical Probability Literacy
description: A micro-lesson that makes Medical Probability Literacy usable.

hook.text: Your doctor says a procedure has a "95% success rate." What does that actually mean for you?

buildup.text: Does it mean 95 out of 100 patients survive? Improve? Have no complications? Definitions vary wildly.

discovery.text: Absolute vs. relative risk matters. A drug "reduces risk by 50%" sounds huge—until the base risk is 0.02%.

twist.text: A 50% relative reduction of 0.02% is 0.01%. The actual benefit is tiny—but the headline sounds massive.

climax.text: Ask for absolute numbers. "5 out of 1,000 vs. 10 out of 1,000" is far clearer than "50% reduction."

quiz.question: Why can relative risk reductions be misleading?
options: They hide how small the base risk is
